analysis: Examined base text of .github/workflows/provider-tests.yml (lines 530-1523) and the patch excerpt. Changes are CI-only: a new cluster_gpu input, build jobs now gated solely on inputs.cluster/provider (no longer building on push when the tree was already tested), test-cluster-gpu gating and runs-on lane changes around lines 916-923, and extra record/gate logic near 1514-1539 (head side; only partly visible in the truncated patch). No provider runtime code, wire protocol, attestation, key handling, or cache-storage code is touched, so the threat IDs for the provider (T-041 prefix cache, TB-011 etc.) are not affected. Workflow security properties visible in base remain: actions pinned to SHAs, persist-credentials false, the cached .git sanity check (symlinks, hooks, fsmonitor/include config), and minimal permissions on gate/plan jobs. Reducing build jobs on already-tested pushes does not weaken gating, because the gate still requires the expected result per the changed flags. Remaining uncertainty: the patch excerpt is truncated, so head-side changes at 916-923 and 1517-1539 (the gate's handling of cluster_gpu, and the record upload) were not fully visible. If the gate drops required checks or the skip logic is loosened, CI integrity would be affected. Also the new cluster_gpu plumbing in provider-plan.yml is out of this batch. No concrete security regression identified from the visible evidence.
